correctness.rationale: Positive reset probability makes every one-step state-to-state transition positive, ensuring a unique invariant law. Conditional next-part A uses only old B and independent fresh randomness, and conditional next-part B only old A; a product law across parts is preserved and uniqueness makes the invariant law a product. On a complete biclique, the A fraction two-step law is the composition of binomial sampling via r(u)=epsilon/2+(1-epsilon)u; total variance gives the exact two-step drift and variance in the source. Scaling by h=1/a+1/b gives limiting Wright–Fisher drift λ(1-2u) and diffusion u(1-u)/2. A uniform third-moment bound allows passing polynomial test functions to the stationary generator; the resulting moments uniquely determine Beta(2λ,2λ). Independent partwise limits then yield product Beta. Pair-spin covariance equations, including the 1/a,1/b finite self-copy terms, settle zero- and high-noise endpoints by second moments. A separate exact-rational K2,2 check preserved cross-part product structure under 35 full synchronous updates; the source exact-rational stationary checker (inspected) verifies K_ab cases more broadly. The finite check is not proof of the limiting law.
residual_risks: No process-level diffusion convergence or rates; the theorem concerns only stationary fraction weak limits.

value.rationale: The precise update protocol creates an unusual exact independence of the entire same-time vertex-part states despite continual cross-part copying. A three-regime joint stationary phase classification at the natural inverse-population noise scale, with two independent nondegenerate Beta limits and no aspect-ratio restriction, differs qualitatively from the known asynchronous common-Beta phenomenon and is mathematically motivated.
residual_risks: The model assumes perfectly simultaneous fair-noise updates; a conventional continuous-time noisy voter process has different correlations and limits.

final_claim: For fair independent synchronous noisy voter updates on every finite bipartite graph without isolated vertices and positive reset noise, the unique stationary law factorizes exactly across the two vertex parts. On K_{a,b}, with a,b tending to infinity at arbitrary relative rates and reset-to-(a^-1+b^-1) ratio λ, the two stationary density limits are independent Zλ, with a fair two-atom law for λ=0, Beta(2λ,2λ) for 0<λ<infinity, and point mass at 1/2 for λ=infinity.
